one_liner: Entry-level grocery store job at a military base commissary: stocking shelves, running checkout, helping customers, and doing basic inventory and ordering paperwork.
fit_summary: Daniel clears the GS-4 experience bar easily, but this retail role with no promotion potential uses none of his emergency management, logistics or public health experience and pays far below his level. Treat it only as a last-resort way into federal service.
eligibility: Open to the public (also military spouses and federal transition candidates), so no prior federal status is needed.
Qualify with 1 year of progressively responsible clerical, office, or other general work, OR two full years of education above high school (transcripts required), OR a combination of the two.
You must attest that you can stand, stoop, kneel, bend, and climb for long periods and lift up to 40 pounds independently.
Security clearance is listed as 'Other'; expect a background check for base access.
Location is 'Multiple Locations'; confirm a commissary near Manassas (e.g., Fort Belvoir, Quantico, Fort Myer) is among the options.
strategy: Before applying, decide whether this fits your goals. Your energy is probably better spent on GS-7/9 program analyst, FEMA, or legislative roles, plus state and local emergency-management jobs.
If he applies, note that the first cut-off (about May 15, 2026) has passed, so later applicants are considered only as new vacancies open.

Frame your IEM work around client communication, document preparation, and administrative tracking, so it maps to the Clerical & Administrative, Communications, and Customer Service competencies. Describe what you actually did.
List hours per week (e.g., 'Full Time' or '40 hours per week') for every job, because the posting says missing hours can make a resume incomplete. Keep it within two pages.
Answer the questionnaire honestly. Overstating checkout or retail experience you lack is grounds for an ineligible rating, and you must be able to back every answer up on your resume.
Do not copy announcement text verbatim, and leave off photos, social media links, and personal data such as age.
resume_bullets: Procured and tracked medical supplies for sites in six states (2021–2022).
Served the public at a five-person intake center for ReBuild NC after Hurricane Matthew (2019).
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you helped a frustrated customer or member of the public.
How do you stay accurate when handling money or records under time pressure?
Can you perform the physical requirements and work varying shifts and occasional overtime?
Why do you want to work at a commissary serving military families?
watch_outs: Low pay ($17.82–$25.95/hr) and no promotion potential make this a poor match for your policy and emergency-management career goals.
The job is physically demanding and on-site only, with no telework, temperature changes, and occasional overtime.
Military spouse and veterans' preference candidates are referred ahead of you within the best-qualified category.
